blockers: Normal daily run for 2026-11-13. GitHub Trending rendered 13 entries; all 13 were reviewed and star counts and default-branch commits verified via the GitHub API.

Six coding-agent-eligible repos (>=3000 stars): addyosmani/agent-skills (5), GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src (4), openai/codex-security (4), QwenLM/qwen-code (4), Alishahryar1/free-claude-code (3), CopilotKit/OpenBot (3). The top five were archived (cap 5 of 5); OpenBot was logged as eligible, not archived (daily cap), without downloading. The other 7 entries were rejected (nvm, Node.js, llama.cpp, a finance app, a design-system library, and two repos below 3,000 stars: pookjw/HermesEnabler 1,548 and ashhart/TensorFold 1,948).

Never re-clone rule applied: unmodified checks passed for all three already-archived repos before the same-volume move. addyosmani/agent-skills was unchanged; codex-security was upgraded 2911786 -> 4822a9c and free-claude-code 4e99dda -> 5662101 by incremental git fetch, previous manifests kept as previous-*.json. free-claude-code was in the legacy 2026-10-13 format (bare object store without refs/origin remote, no archive-result.json), so it was checked with check_unmodified_legacy.py and upgraded with upgrade_legacy.py (same method, fetch from its public HTTPS URL). No user-edited copies found.

Two partial clones of GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src started with a mistyped (non-API) commit SHA were stopped before completing and moved to the volume Trash via NSFileManager (recoverable; not permanently deleted); the final snapshot was cloned with the API-verified SHA 3bb177a and fully verified. GitHub now reports free-claude-code's license as NOASSERTION (was AGPL-3.0-only on 2026-10-13).
git-lfs is still not installed on this Mac; none of today's archived trees contain LFS pointers. Repository code, hooks, installers and dependencies were never run.

Two new featured recommendations: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src and QwenLM/qwen-code (never featured). The other archived repos were featured earlier (agent-skills, codex-security, free-claude-code).

featured.reason: Modern Web Guidance (Apache-2.0), stewarded by the Chrome, Edge, Firefox and MDN teams: the source repo for an Agent Skill and CLI (`npx modern-web-guidance search / retrieve / legacy-scan`) that feeds coding agents token-efficient guides on ~250 modern web features (CSS layout, View Transitions, Popover/anchor positioning, INP and loading performance, accessibility, built-in AI, WebMCP), plus the Playwright-based eval harness that measures Claude Code and other agents. Rated 4 rather than 5 because this is the authoring/eval source; the installable skill is published from GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance. Now 3,075 verified stars (was 1,800 and below the threshold yesterday).
ideas: Run `npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan .` on ai-daily-radar to list legacy patterns, then have your agent fix them in small commits while keeping the site's original design.

Install the skill in Claude Code or Codex (`npx skills add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance` or `gh skill install GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance`) and point it at the performance guides (break-up-long-tasks, identify-inp-causes, defer-rendering-heavy-content) to keep the animated background smooth on your phone and in the Android WebView.

Before touching UI controls such as the top-right language switch, `search` the ui-components and forms guides (Popover API, anchor positioning, dialogs) so the agent uses native, keyboard-accessible patterns instead of extra JavaScript.
Read guides/webmcp (agentic-forms, agentic-javascript-tools) to explore exposing the site's daily data and filters as WebMCP tools that browser agents can call directly.

Study docs/EVALS.md and src/harness: it runs Claude Code and other agents against Playwright outcome checks. Copy the approach to test whether your shared skills, such as CLI-Anything, actually change what agents produce.

featured.reason: Qwen Code (Apache-2.0): an open-source terminal coding agent (Qwen Code 1.0 Preview) with skills, subagents, agent teams, hooks, MCP, plan mode and LSP; works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen APIs or local models (Ollama/vLLM); headless `qwen -p`, TypeScript/Python/Java SDKs, `qwen serve` daemon (HTTP+SSE/ACP, Web UI), IDE plugins and Telegram/DingTalk/WeChat/Feishu channels. Rated 4: a full alternative/companion harness to Claude Code and Codex, but it needs a provider account or local model, and the daemon has no auth by default unless QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN is set.
ideas: Point Qwen Code at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or a local Ollama/vLLM model and give it the same small ai-daily-radar task as Claude Code and Codex to compare quality, speed and cost.
Use headless `qwen -p "..."` in a script or CI job for cheap, repeatable chores such as checking the publish output or drafting changelog notes, keeping your main agents for harder work.
Run `qwen serve --open` on the Mac mini with QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN set (the daemon has no auth by default) and use the Web UI from your Android phone to start and review coding sessions.
Connect one of the chat channels (Telegram, WeChat, DingTalk or Feishu) so you can send a coding task from your phone and get the result back in chat.

Explore the TypeScript/Python SDKs and the ACP route (the qwen-code-claw skill via acpx) to let Claude Code or Codex hand sub-tasks to Qwen Code as a second worker; packages/cua-driver also shows how its computer-use MCP tools are wired.

news_highlights.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Google's new fast model for coding and agent work is available on every Gemini API tier at a flat $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens across a 1M context, with four thinking levels. It is a cheap option for the execution steps in agent pipelines.

news_highlights.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Antigravity's Orchestrator switches between Carbon (planning) and Hydrogen (edits and tests) within one session. Google reports near-Carbon success on Terminal-Bench with 24% less quota and 19% faster runs. It is the same advisor/executor split you can set up yourself with cheaper models.

news_highlights.title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
news_highlights.why_it_matters: GitHub's guide to portable SKILL.md skills: keep project details in a manifest, use one execution path, add human checkpoints, and generate Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot packaging from a single source with a CI check. Useful for keeping shared skills in sync across your bots.

news_highlights.title: Turning a 22-year-old Postgres type-confusion primitive into RCE
news_highlights.why_it_matters: CVE-2026-6460 lets a low-privileged login role reach code execution with PREPARE plus ALTER TYPE on composite types. It was fixed in PostgreSQL's 9 November release (52 CVEs), and the author reports every managed Postgres vendor he tested was affected. Patch any Postgres you run.

news_highlights.title: Anthropic IPO
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Anthropic's IPO site reports Q3'26 revenue of $17.0B (more than 12x year over year) and says pricing is expected on November 18 and trading on Nasdaq as "ANT" on November 19 (EST). This is a major market event for the company behind Claude Code.
